newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent gains hit by profit-taking into the closE.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent gains hit by profit-taking into the closE.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures ended almost unchanged on Monday after profit-taking wiped out earlier gains on a refinery problem in the United States, brokers said.
December Brent closed at $24.16 per barrel, six cents below Friday's settlement.
"There's just some profit-taking on the close," a broker said. He added that selling presure was particularly strong on the MYMEX oil products futures, which are due to expire on Thursday.

Earlier gains were attributed to a valve fault at Amoco's 433,000 barrel per day (bpd) Texas City refinery which hit operation of a 204,000 bpd catcracker at the site, regulators said. Traders said this forced Amoco to buy gasoline heavily on the U.S. Gulf coast spot market.
November gas oil closed $2.75 higher at $227.00 per tonne. Gas oil trade was thin and the Dec Brant/gas oil crack spread was steady at $5.25 per barrel.
While December Brent fell sharply into the close, January Brent held on to some of its early gain to close up 14 cents at $23.60 per barrel.

Traders said the Dec/Jan spread was under pressure from very weak demand for wet Brent. Dec/Jan fell 20 cents on the day to close at +60 cents after Dated Brent traded at six cents below December paper, compared to Thursday's trade at Dec +44 cents.
